Test phylogenetic beta diversity against the environment

Source: R/phylo_beta.R
phylo_beta_test.Rd

Implements the phylogenetic beta-diversity framework of Peres-Neto & Kembel (2015), a distance-based redundancy analysis (Legendre & Anderson 1999; McArdle & Anderson 2001) of phylo_beta() on the predictors. The test statistic is the pseudo-F. It is tested by permuting sites, which breaks the link between composition and environment, and by permuting species across the tips, which breaks the link between composition and phylogeny. The association requires both, so the p-value to report is the larger of the two.

Usage

phylo_beta_test(comm, tree, env, n_perm = 999, site_permutations = NULL)

Arguments

comm

Matrix with one row per site and one column per species, named as the tips of tree. Every site needs at least one individual.

tree

A phylo object with the same species as comm.

env

Predictor, or matrix or data frame of predictors, with one row per site.

n_perm

Number of permutations of sites and of species.

site_permutations

Optional matrix of site indices with one permutation per row, for example from torus_permutations(), to use instead of free permutations of sites.

Value

List of class mc_phylo_beta with r2, the adjusted R2; statistic, the pseudo-F; p_site, p_taxa and p_max; and scores, the sites on the principal coordinates of the predicted matrix, which the authors suggest using to order sites in a heatmap of the community matrix.

Details

The equations printed in the article omit the 1 in the adjusted R2, the transpose in the hat matrix and the centring of the matrix that is regressed. Here the predictors and the matrix are centred, and the residual degrees of freedom are n - p - 1, with n - 1 for the total, instead of the printed n - p and n. The pseudo-F and R2 therefore equal those of a distance-based redundancy analysis in vegan. The printed degrees of freedom would multiply the pseudo-F by a constant, which does not change the permutation tests.

The authors used presences and absences. Abundances are accepted, as weights in phylo_beta().

References

Legendre, P., & Anderson, M. J. (1999). Distance-based redundancy analysis: testing multispecies responses in multifactorial ecological experiments. Ecological Monographs, 69, 1–24. doi:10.1890/0012-9615(1999)069[0001:DBRATM]2.0.CO;2

McArdle, B. H., & Anderson, M. J. (2001). Fitting multivariate models to community data: a comment on distance-based redundancy analysis. Ecology, 82, 290–297. doi:10.1890/0012-9658(2001)082[0290:FMMTCD]2.0.CO;2

Peres-Neto, P. R., & Kembel, S. W. (2015). Phylogenetic gradient analysis: environmental drivers of phylogenetic variation across ecological communities. Plant Ecology, 216, 709–724. doi:10.1007/s11258-014-0405-0

See also

pcc_test(), the other framework of the same article.

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- ape::rcoal(20)
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(-1, 101),
                         rmax_range = c(0, 30))
env <- runif(50, 0, 100)
comm <- simulate_static(traits, env, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
keep <- rowSums(comm) > 0
phylo_beta_test(comm[keep, ], tree, env[keep], n_perm = 99)
#> <mc_phylo_beta> phylogenetic beta diversity
#> adjusted R2: 0.315  pseudo-F: 23.6 
#> p (sites): 0.01  p (species): 0.01  p (max): 0.01
